subject: Allocation and posting plan for promotional credit across multiple invoices
body:
From: Anita Bose <anita.bose@starlane.io>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request to apply promotional credit across two outstanding invoices

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the pilot — the team saw strong latency wins. Finance asked me to follow up: we were issued a $12,500 promotional credit tied to the pilot. We have two unpaid invoices on our account (INV-2027-331 for $8,900; INV-2027-350 for $6,700). Can Redwood either:

- Apply the credit across both invoices (split by outstanding balance), or
- Issue a single credit memo for $12,500 to be applied to future invoices (please indicate posting and GL treatment),

We need a short note for our auditors showing the accounting treatment and timeline. I attached the credit request and our invoice list. Can you advise what you plan to do and when it will show on our account?

Best,
Anita Bose
Finance Lead, Starlane AI
billing@starlane.io

-----
Attachment: starlane_credit_request_0827.pdf (pdf)

---
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anita Bose <anita.bose@starlane.io>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request to apply promotional credit across two outstanding invoices

Team — forwarding Starlane's ask. Key points: $12,500 promo credit; two open invoices (INV-2027-331 $8,900; INV-2027-350 $6,700). External wants either split now or single credit memo.

Questions for finance/accounting:
- Preferred posting: issue credit memo (contra revenue) or net against invoices (invoice offset)? Any G/L mapping we must follow?
- If we split, do we need two credit memos or one memo with allocation schedule?
- Any timing constraints for recognition / revenue reversals (they asked for auditor note).

I've drafted a proposed credit memo (proposed-credit-memo_kp_0830.pdf) that shows $8,900 applied to INV-2027-331 and $3,600 applied to INV-2027-350 (leaving $3,100 balance to next billing cycle). Marcus/Neha — can you confirm journal entries and whether we should record an interim liability instead of immediate contra?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

-----
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anita Bose <anita.bose@starlane.io>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request to apply promotional credit across two outstanding invoices

Kimberly / team,

Thanks for the context and the draft memo. From an accounting perspective, recommend the following approach to keep audit trail clean:

1) Issue a single credit memo for $12,500 referencing the two invoices. The credit memo will be posted to contra-revenue (GL: 4005-CONTRA) at issuance date.

2) Simultaneously record a short-term liability account for promotional allowances if the credit is promotional (GL: 2402-PROMO-LIAB) and amortize to contra-revenue as it is applied to an invoice. This avoids immediate revenue reversal if the credit is contingent on future performance.

3) Create allocation schedule showing:
   - $8,900 applied to INV-2027-331 (effective application date 2027-08-31)
   - $3,600 applied to INV-2027-350 (effective application date 2027-09-05)
   - Remaining $0 if fully consumed; if any remainder, carry in promo liability to next invoice.

4) For internal posting: debit 2402-PROMO-LIAB; credit 4005-CONTRA when credit memo is issued. When applied to an invoice: debit 4005-CONTRA; credit AR (or reduce receivable) — or if we net, update invoice status in billing system and generate corresponding adjusting entry.

I've attached GL mapping (GL_mapping_promos_0829.xlsx) with suggested account codes and a sample journal entry. If legal wants separate memos we can issue multiple memos but a single memo with allocation schedule is clearer for the customer and auditors.

Let me know if you want us to proceed with the single credit memo + allocation schedule and we'll coordinate ERP posting and the status change in the billing UI.

-Marcus
Director, Revenue Operations
-----
Attachment: GL_mapping_promos_0829.xlsx (xlsx)

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2027 15:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request to apply promotional credit across two outstanding invoices

Hi Anita — looping back with final plan (per Marcus' recommendation):

1) We'll issue a single credit memo for $12,500 today (CM-2027-114). The memo will reference INV-2027-331 and INV-2027-350 and include an allocation schedule.

2) Accounting treatment: Redwood will post the memo to contra-revenue (GL 4005-CONTRA) and, given the promotional nature, record in promo liability (GL 2402) pending application. Application schedule: $8,900 applied to INV-2027-331 effective 2027-08-31; $3,600 applied to INV-2027-350 effective 2027-09-05. Any remaining balance would stay in promo liability until invoiced.

3) You'll receive a PDF copy of the credit memo and a short audit note showing journal entries and dates. Expect the memo and audit note in your inbox by EOD PT.

If that works I'll proceed and mark the invoices as partially paid in the billing system so your AR reflects the adjustment.

Thanks for the patience — appreciate the partnership during the pilot.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
